title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZT (Power to modify Act in its application to Producer Companies)

content.overview: Section 378ZT permits the Central Government, by notification, to direct that specified provisions of the Companies Act outside Chapter XXIA either do not apply to Producer Companies or apply with specified exceptions or adaptations. The section also provides for the proposed notification to be laid in draft before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days, subject to the section's stated disapproval or modification process.
content.glance: The Central Government may issue a section 378ZT notification specifying whether provisions outside Chapter XXIA do not apply to Producer Companies or apply with specified exceptions or adaptations, subject to the statutory parliamentary process.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZT (Power to modify Act in its application to Producer Companies). The Central Government may, by notification, direct that specified provisions of the Act outside Chapter XXIA shall not apply to Producer Companies or shall apply with specified exceptions or adaptations. The proposed notification is subject to the draft-laying and parliamentary disapproval/modification process stated in the section. A specific modification must be established from the applicable notification; do not infer one merely from the enabling provision. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Notification power
sections.body: The Central Government may, by notification, direct that specified provisions of the Act other than those in Chapter XXIA shall not apply to Producer Companies or shall apply with specified exceptions or adaptations.

sections.heading: Parliamentary process
sections.body: The section requires a copy of the proposed notification to be laid in draft before each House of Parliament for a total period of thirty days, which may be comprised in one session or in two or more successive sessions. The section states the consequences where both Houses disapprove the issue or agree on modifications before expiry of the relevant following session.

sections.heading: Scope note
sections.body: The existence and effect of a particular modification depend on the relevant notification and the statutory process. Do not assume a provision has been excluded or adapted without checking the applicable instrument and its current status.

examples.title: Checking an asserted modification
examples.body: Where a party asserts that a provision outside Chapter XXIA applies to a Producer Company with an exception or adaptation, identify the section 378ZT notification relied on and verify its text, parliamentary process and current applicability.

hypotheticals.question: What must be checked before asserting that a provision of the Companies Act applies differently to a Producer Company under section 378ZT?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify the specific notification, the provision it addresses, the exception or adaptation stated, and evidence of the statutory process and current applicability. Section 378ZT alone does not identify which provisions have actually been modified.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the section 378ZT notification power as identical to the section 378ZU rule-making power.
misconceptions.correction: Identify the instrument and statutory power actually relied on; notification-based modification and chapter rule-making are distinct.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring the parliamentary draft-laying and disapproval/modification procedure in section 378ZT.
misconceptions.correction: Check the statutory process described in section 378ZT before treating a proposed notification as effective in the form asserted.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 378zt do?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The Central Government may, by notification, direct that any of the provisions of the Act shall apply to a Producer Company with such exceptions, modifications and adaptations as may be specified.
